transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-18
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Liu (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (CTO, Sentinel), Ben Torres (Sr Engineer), Liam O'Connor (Product), Nina (SRE), Jake (Intern)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on PLG/self-serve Redwood API path: time-to-first-token, free credits, integration steps. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for a doc-intelligence product; primary concerns: latency, cost, data residency/compliance, and dev velocity. Agreed next steps: send quickstart + credits, schedule SE sandbox, share security docs and preliminary Dedicated sizing/pricing.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. quick intros, i'll kick it off; i'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account.
00:07 Aisha: Hi this is Aisha, CTO at Sentinel Systems. we build a document intelligence product for regulated industries, lots of PII.
00:12 Ben: Ben here, sr eng, i'll be hands on with the integration.
00:15 Liam: Liam, product, interested in how fast we can get a prototype live.
00:19 Carlos: Carlos from Redwood, i'm the solutions engineer; i'll run through architecture and performance questions.
00:25 Maya: Great. high level, are you folks thinking about a self-serve quickstart path first or do you expect to go direct to Dedicated/Private?
00:33 Aisha: We want to move fast — prototype via self-serve / free credits is ideal, but long term we need either Dedicated or Private for data residency and KMS integration.
00:42 Ben: Agree. dev velocity matters, but the end state is compliant hosting — possibly VPC or on-prem.
00:48 Maya: That's totally normal. our PLG quickstart is aimed exactly at time-to-first-token: sign up, free credits, get an API key, sample prompts and an SDK quickstart to call generation and embeddings. Typically teams have a prototype in hours.
01:02 Jake: Quick question — do you provide sample prompts for doc extraction?
01:05 Carlos: yes, we have starter prompt sets and eval harnesses; we'll share the repo link in follow up.
01:12 Ben: On latency: for multi-page doc processing we need token-level latency to be under ~1s average per request if batched, otherwise it affects UX. can Redwood hit that on Hosted?
01:24 Carlos: For Hosted API with our recommended model families, sub-second tail latency for typical document calls is achievable with streaming off, and we do have per-route model profiles. obviously depends on model size and token counts.
01:37 Liam: Price is a big factor; how do we estimate cost for high-volume embedding generation?
01:43 Maya: We provide per-token pricing for Hosted. for embeddings we also surface unit pricing; Redwood Optimize gives recommendations (batching, quantization suggestions) to reduce unit cost. we'll send a sample cost projection template.
01:56 Aisha: Security: SOC 2, SSO, audit logs, KMS — do you support customer-managed keys in Dedicated/Private?
02:05 Carlos: yes. Dedicated and Private both support KMS integrations and HSM options in Private. we have audit logs + RBAC; i'll attach the security whitepaper.
02:15 Ben: For Dedicated, what's the lead time and is autoscaling supported?
02:20 Maya: Dedicated is reserved capacity, lead time depends on commitment but usually weeks; autoscaling policies are configurable and we have burst capacity options.
02:28 Ben: We might want a short pilot — reserve a small Dedicated pool or do a fully hosted pilot?
02:33 Carlos: Most customers start hosted for quick benchmarking, then move to Dedicated once they hit predictable throughput. we can also do a private pilot if you have strict compliance.
02:41 Liam: What's the time to first token for the PLG quickstart? i.e., from sign up to actually hitting the API.
02:46 Maya: From sign up to first token is typically under 30 minutes: account creation, API key in console, run the quickstart script. with our SDK the code sample is 5 lines.
02:55 Jake: Are there usage quotas on free credits?
02:58 Maya: Yes, free credits have caps to prevent abuse but are generous enough for prototyping — we'll share exact amounts in the follow up.
03:05 Aisha: We have an internal compliance checklist — data retention rules, ability to delete logs, and regional hosting for EMEA. how does Redwood handle data retention on Hosted?
03:17 Carlos: For Hosted we have retention controls and can set zero retention for specific customers on request; for full data isolation and residency we recommend Dedicated or Private. i'll include the retention matrix doc.
03:28 Ben: On the technical side, we run on EKS and have an MLOps stack that expects model endpoints. how invasive is integrating Redwood SDK?
03:36 Carlos: Integration is minimal for PLG path: SDK calls or direct REST. for Dedicated/Private we provide connectors and orchestration templates; not invasive.
03:44 Liam: Any gotchas with embeddings consistency across model versions? we want stable vectors for search.
03:49 Carlos: We recommend pinning model versions and using Redwood-verified model profiles; Optimize has drift detection and alerts if embeddings regress.
03:58 Aisha: Can we run a benchmark with our dataset? Ben would like to run throughput and latency tests.
04:04 Ben: Yep, we'll prepare a representative sample set.
04:07 Carlos: Great — we can set up a sandbox with a temporary key and reserved slot for benchmarking.
04:13 Maya: Next, procurement questions — do you have standard contract term expectations?
04:17 Aisha: For enterprise we need an annual commitment with SLA; for POC quickstart, a simple TOS is fine.
04:24 Maya: Noted. we'll share contract templates.
04:28 Liam: Is there a way to do a canary rollout for a model change in production?
04:32 Carlos: Yes — rollouts support canary and A/B, and automatic fallback to previous model variants.
04:37 Ben: On cost control, can we set per-route quotas or token budgets?
04:41 Maya: Yes, per-route rate limits, budget alerts, and token-level cost breakdowns in Console.
04:48 Jake: Are there SDKs for node and python?
04:50 Maya: Both, plus a Go client beta.
04:54 Aisha: For Private deployment, what's the typical on-prem footprint for our use case? we process roughly 5k docs/day, peaks to 20k.
05:02 Carlos: That workload could fit on a modest cluster; we'll propose a sizing estimate. Private on-prem footprints vary by model choice and quantization; we'll include a sizing matrix.
05:13 Ben: Any examples of customers in regulated industries?
05:16 Maya: Yes — several finance and healthcare customers; we'll anonymize case studies and send links.
05:21 Liam: Ok, practical: can you send the quickstart guide, the free credits link, security pack, and a sample cost projection?
05:28 Maya: Absolutely — i'll send an email after the call. Carlos will schedule the sandbox/demo.
05:32 Carlos: i'll follow up with a calendar invite for a SE-led sandbox next week; can we target tuesday or wednesday?
05:39 Aisha: Wednesday works for Ben and me.
05:42 Maya: Great. any final questions?
05:45 Ben: One small thing — when you said zero retention, does that mean you don't persist requests by default? sometimes transcription implies logs are stored.
05:52 Carlos: default Hosted keeps logs for debugging, but we have zero-retention options and for Dedicated/Private logs are customer-managed. i'll include explicit wording in the security doc.
06:02 Aisha: Perfect. thanks everyone.
06:05 Maya: Thanks all. we'll follow up with the docs and invites.

- Maya to send PLG quickstart link + free credits, quickstart repo, pricing template, and security whitepaper (due 2026-05-19).
